entry.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
entry.summary: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

entry.title: DIY fertilizer is a blessing as farmers face steep prices due to the Iran war
entry.summary: It's hard enough being a small-scale farmer. Then the Iran war drove up fertilizer prices. So farmers are using a traditional Asian recipe to make their own. They call it a "labor of love."

entry.title: An early flu season means it might be time to think about a flu shot
entry.summary: Flu season typically starts in October or November. But it looks like the flu started to pick up in September this year.

entry.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
entry.summary: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.

entry.title: 5 things civil rights data says about public schools
entry.summary: The federal Civil Rights Data Collection, for the first time in decades, tells us about the teacher workforce and reminds us racial disparities are still stark in American public schools.

entry.title: An early start to flu season moves up vaccination timing
entry.summary: This year's flu season is unusual. It started early and in the West, instead of the South. A new variant with a mutation that helps the virus evade immunity may be playing a role.

entry.title: What happened during Christa Pike's failed execution
entry.summary: Catherine Sweeney was in the witness room when Tennessee attempted to execute Christa Pike on Sept. 30. An attempted execution in May had also failed. Here's what Sweeney saw and heard.

entry.title: Wildfire smoke affects animals in unique ways. Scientists are trying to understand it
entry.summary: The new field of "smoke ecology" examines how wildfire smoke perturbs wild places and animals — and what might be done to prevent its worst mayhem.

entry.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
entry.summary: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating them now.

entry.title: From floating saunas to clinical trials: How heat might help mental health
entry.summary: While scientists have a decent understanding of how sauna and other forms of heat exposure exercises our cardiovascular system, they know relatively little about its impact on mental health.
